mappings.note: Who said 'I will tie the ganda only on receiving the offering' -- attribution of a quoted line. Rejected LO-107: the item asks who spoke, not what the custom is.
To whose singing he danced long on request (Suraiya) -- biographical detail. Rejected LO-107: a name, not the art.
How many kathik households Hariya village held (989) -- a located figure. Rejected LO-106: the number, not the village's folk story.
From whom he inherited the art of Kathak (his forebears) -- the transmission of the form. Rejected LO-105: about the tradition, not a single fact of his life.
What he liked doing in free time -- opening machines, painting seventy pictures. Rejected LO-107: pursuits outside the dance.
How his mother helped through the struggle -- loans and burning zari saris, both narrated. Rejected LO-100: the item asks what she did, not about women's position.
What he did alongside dancing -- played, sang, composed dance-dramas and their music: the range of the art. Rejected LO-105: about his practice of the form.
The place of lay in dance -- keyed to body, meditation, austerity and balance, the central technical idea of the interview. Rejected LO-102: the answer is about the art, not a social claim.
Why he recommends that children play with lay -- his argument about intellectual growth. Rejected LO-107: the reasoning is about children, not about technique.
His full name (Brijmohan Mishra) -- biographical. Rejected LO-107: a name.
What he gave his father as the offering -- the dakshina for two gandas, part of the art's initiation custom. Rejected LO-105: the custom carries the item.
Which instruments he learnt -- sitar, guitar, sarod, tabla: the instruments of the tradition. Rejected LO-105: the instruments, not a date.
How neck and fingers are moved in Kathak -- the technique itself, likened to a lamp flame. The clearest case in the chapter for the dance-craft outcome. Rejected LO-105: a matter of practice.
The guru-pupil custom at the start of training -- ganda and offering. Rejected LO-105: the custom of the art.
What Kathak's older form was like -- informal story-telling. Rejected LO-106: it is the classical form's history, not folk material of the learner's own surroundings.
Why he made Kathak pieces from poets of many languages -- his reason, that languages differ but people are alike everywhere. Rejected LO-107: the ground is a human claim, not a technical one.
What his uncle said when he took a job -- a quoted remark. Rejected LO-102, kept for the item asking what he then resolved.
From whom he had his training -- three named teachers. Rejected LO-107: names, not the art.
The chief classical dance styles -- Kathak, Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi and the rest: knowledge of the forms. Rejected LO-105: about the arts, not the man.
Describe his childhood struggles -- the money troubles, narrated. Rejected LO-110: the account is the text's, not the learner's own experience.
How his training with his guru began -- the ganda withheld until the offering came, and his mother's earnings. Rejected LO-105: the initiation custom carries the answer.
The place of music in learning dance and how it keeps balance -- lay as the joining idea. Rejected LO-102: the claim is about the art.
Which changes he made to Kathak performance -- tradition kept, presentation altered, his elders' bearing taken in. Rejected LO-105: about the form.
Why he called tradition a TREE -- the ground of his figure, that it shelters all alike. Rejected LO-107: a metaphor about tradition, not a technical term.
Which struggles he faced -- his father's death, poverty, riyaz kept up. Rejected LO-110: the text's account, not the learner's own.
What Kathak's early presentation was like -- temple story-telling, later the courts. Rejected LO-105: the form's history.
What his uncles and father were to him -- gurus and guides. Rejected LO-102: a located relation.

How we can tell he backed teaching girls Kathak, and his views on it -- his sisters untaught, his daughters taught, and the claim that girls need a skill. Gender is named in this outcome, so this is its proper home. Rejected LO-103: the learner sets out his position rather than arguing a preference of their own.

Why knowing lay matters -- the key runs from music and dance out to every activity of life, but the term and its use belong to the art. Rejected LO-102: lay is a technical concept before it is a life lesson.

The difference between folk and classical dance -- collective and for its own satisfaction against solo and for an audience. Rejected LO-106: the item compares two forms rather than appreciating folk material as such.

Where Hariya village lies and the story attached to the Bairgiya nala -- nine kathiks, three robbers, and the art that made the robbers forget themselves. That is a local folk legend, which is exactly what this outcome covers. Rejected LO-105: the item asks for the story, not a fact.
His appeal to parents about children's interests -- his argument that art teaches balance, timing and cooperation. Rejected LO-107: addressed to parents, not about technique.
Substantiate that he was many-sided -- the learner gathers the evidence: composing, singing, tabla, painting, machines. Rejected LO-103: the claim is given, not chosen by the learner.
Why he altered the ganda custom -- testing dedication before tying it. A change to a practice of the art. Rejected LO-102: the custom is the subject.

'Write an article' on his life and his devotion to dance -- a composition in the learner's own style, which is what this outcome covers. Rejected LO-105: the demand is a piece of writing, not retrieval. NOTE: the stored key is a short paragraph identical to an earlier item's answer, far short of an article.
Describe Kathak's tradition and the changes in it -- the form's history. Rejected LO-105: about the art. NOTE: the stored key repeats an earlier item's answer verbatim.

Explain his views on the importance of art AND write them in your own words -- the composition in the learner's own voice is the stated demand. Rejected LO-102, which would fit if only comprehension were wanted. NOTE: the stored key answers a different question entirely, about who his gurus were.

Which interviewer wanted to know the difference between the two forms -- the item turns on who put the question, i.e. on the interview's structure of questioning for better understanding. Rejected LO-107: the dance content is asked in its own items.
What folk dance is like (collective), from the printed extract. Rejected LO-106: the item asks the defining mark, not appreciation of folk material.
Whom classical dance is for (the audience) -- the distinguishing point of the form. Rejected LO-105: about the art.
